header.title: How to Unclog a Dishwasher Drain
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to diagnose and clear common clogs in a dishwasher drain. Follow these steps to restore your dishwasher's functionality and prevent future drainage issues.

steps.description: Ensure the dishwasher, garbage disposal, and their respective electrical circuits are completely shut off at the breaker panel before proceeding.
actions: Shut off dishwasher
Shut off garbage disposal
Turn off electricity to dishwasher at the breaker
Turn off electricity to garbage disposal at the breaker
Confirm everything is turned off
steps.part: Breaker(s) in the main electric panel

steps.description: This step involves checking the dishwasher's drain hose for clogs by disconnecting it, snaking it, and reconnecting it.
actions: Locate the dishwasher's drain hose connection to the sink or garbage disposal drain pipe.
Pull the dishwasher out or locate the hose under the sink.
Loosen the pipe clamp.
Disconnect the hose.
Insert a drain snake into the hose.
Dislodge and extract the source of the clog.
Reconnect the hose.
Re-fasten the clamp.

steps.description: Check the dishwasher drain for clogs by removing filters and extracting foreign objects, and if necessary, use baking soda and vinegar to dislodge them.
actions: Consult dishwasher's owner's manual to locate the drain.
Remove the drain catch and filters.
Use a plastic spoon or non-metallic blade to dig around inside the drain.
Extract any foreign objects lodged in and obstructing the drain pathway.
Pour one tablespoon of baking soda down the dishwasher's drain.
Pour two tablespoons of vinegar down the dishwasher's drain.

steps.description: Reconnect the drain catch and filters, then turn the dishwasher and garbage disposal power back on.
actions: Reconnect drain catch
Reconnect filters
Turn on dishwasher power
Turn on garbage disposal power
